reviews.review: Immensely difficult, immensely fun, and immensely addicting, Risk of Rain is easily my surprise favorite game of the season. I have easily put in 22 hours since I bought it during the holiday sale, and I've been playing a lot of co-op as well. Unfortunately, the game uses direct IP connect for multiplayer and zero mod support, but other than that and some latency, I've had no issues with it. You unlock something on every playthrough, even tens of hours later. The characters are unique and play very differently from one another, synergizing well with different skills. Artifacts (togglable game modifiers) are an interesting touch that change the game too. Risk of Rain is easily worth your time, and remember to play with a controller.

This is the sort of game you play when you have hours available, so you can try again repeatedly to see how many more Fedex containers you can hijack before the government lizards chase you down and interrogate you for cargo theft.

This game is brutal. It punishes you for being slow. It punishes you (slightly less) for being fast. You're not going to coast, no matter what items you collect or which class you play, which is perfect for this type of game. If I have one complaint it's that collectables don't significantly alter gameplay style, and there's a relatively small variety of bosses, so it doesn't have quite the level of replayability of games like The Binding of Isaac, FTL or Dungeons of Dredmore. It makes up for that, though, by being fast paced and fun.

Extremely addictive. You'll find yourself playing this game for hours on end.

First of all, Risk of Rain is a platformer with roguelike elements that never gets old. Every new game you start will be different from the last one you played. 

Now, Personally I really loved this game because of its genre: survival-esque combined with perk-gathering. Your goal is to survive for as long as possible through levels while opening chests containing perks (items that will 'boost' your character, whether it be a goat hoof that increases your movement speed to a flask of liquid that boosts your health regen, there are just a ton of different items with different abilities).

As for gameplay, the game itself isn't that hard. It only takes about 90 minutes, give or take, to beat the game, solo. But what makes you come back to it are all the unlockable items, classes and artifacts that completely change a game that you think would be unchangable.

This the perfect game for fans of survival/scavenging/platformer -esque games
10/10 do recommend
